risks.risk: Model mismatch (wrong AR-M201 or different Sharp variant), which changes parts availability and pricing.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model/serial label (usually rear/inside door) with the text readable.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic Sharp all-in-one copier with unknown exact model; worst-case parts/compatibility risk.

risks.risk: Not truly fully functional (hidden faults like fuser issues, scanning problems, or intermittent jams).
risks.proof: Short video of a full copy/print cycle from start to finished output (including no error message).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not guaranteed working; worst-case treated as needing service.

risks.risk: Page count claim may be false; wear could be higher (drum/fuser life).
risks.proof: Photo of the machine’s total counter/page count screen (or service menu page) showing the number.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as higher-wear used equipment (worst-case for consumables).

risks.risk: “New drum and toner” may be generic/incorrect or not properly seated, causing image defects or early failure.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the installed drum/toner labels/part numbers and a test page showing clean output (no streaks/ghosting).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unknown consumables condition; worst-case assumes image quality may be poor.

risks.risk: Paper path/jam issues may appear only under load or with certain paper sizes.
risks.proof: Test with at least 10–20 sheets of the same size (show feeding and continuous output without jam).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potential jam risk; worst-case assumes jams may occur.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the model/serial label with readable text (confirm AR-M201).
Photo of the page/copy counter screen showing the total count.
Video of a complete copy/print test (start → output) with no error messages.
Close-up photos of the installed drum and toner (part labels/compatibility) plus a test print showing image quality.
response.reason: The photos confirm it’s a Sharp all-in-one copier/printer, but the key pricing drivers (exact model, page count, and verified jam-free fully functional test) are not provable from the images. Missing counter and test output means a worst-case price can’t be confidently set without proof.
